title: Make-Ahead Chocolate Soufflés
headnote: From a printed recipe in the family files. The soufflés are filled and frozen in their ramekins up to two days ahead, then baked straight from the freezer — no last-minute whipping while guests are at the table.

items.raw: 5 tablespoons unsalted butter — 1 tablespoon softened, the rest cut into ¼-inch pieces
⅓ cup (65 g) sugar, plus 1 tablespoon for the ramekins
8 ounces (225 g) bittersweet or semisweet chocolate, chopped
1 tablespoon orange liqueur, preferably Grand Marnier

steps.text: Coat eight 1-cup ramekins with the softened butter, then with the 1 tablespoon sugar. Refrigerate.
Melt the chocolate and remaining butter in a bowl set over simmering water. Off the heat, stir in the salt, vanilla, and liqueur.

Bring the ⅓ cup sugar and 2 tablespoons water to a boil and simmer until the sugar dissolves. With the mixer running, slowly pour the syrup into the yolks and beat until tripled in volume, about 3 minutes. Fold into the chocolate. Clean the beaters.
Beat the whites until frothy, add the cream of tartar, and beat to soft peaks. Add the confectioners’ sugar and beat to stiff peaks — firm enough to hold the weight of an egg in its shell set on top.
Vigorously stir a quarter of the whites into the chocolate, then gently fold in the rest until just combined. Fill each ramekin almost to the rim and wipe the rims clean.
Cover and freeze until firm, at least 3 hours and up to 2 days.

Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the lower-middle position. Bake the frozen soufflés 16 to 18 minutes, until fragrant and fully risen. Pull one open with two spoons to peek; if it is not done, return it to the oven. Serve immediately.

notes.label: Individual soufflés only
notes.text: the freezer method does not work for one large soufflé.

notes.label: Mocha version
notes.text: dissolve 1 tablespoon instant coffee in 1 tablespoon hot water and add it with the vanilla.

notes.label: Microwave melting
notes.text: melt the chocolate at 50 percent power for 3 minutes, stirring in the butter after 2.

notes.label: At the table
notes.text: break the tops with a spoon and pour in a little cold cream.

openQuestion: Who makes these, and for what occasion? The printout looks like it came from Cook’s Illustrated — can you confirm?
